metadata.title: Matrix Reasoning IQ Test: 3 Worked Examples
metadata.description: Solve IQ matrix questions: 3 original examples to check rules, split features and reject options; FermatMind's free 30Q practice, free results and score limits.

faq_items.question: Is a matrix reasoning test the same as a complete IQ assessment?
faq_items.answer: No. Matrix questions focus on relationships in visual patterns. A broader cognitive assessment can include other tasks and requires evidence for its intended interpretation. FermatMind's original 30-question online form is reasoning practice and does not replace professional assessment.

faq_items.question: Are the FermatMind test and results both free?
faq_items.answer: Yes. The current original 30-question test and its results are free. Allow about 20 minutes; actual time varies. The worked examples in this article are separate teaching material, not answers to the test bank.

faq_items.question: Should I always add the shapes or rotate them?
faq_items.answer: No. Those are possible relationships, not universal rules. Check any proposed operation against the completed cells. A rule that fails a known row should be rejected, even if an answer option looks plausible.

faq_items.question: Do these examples reveal the answers to the real test?
faq_items.answer: No. They were created for this article to demonstrate checking a rule, separating features and rejecting an option. They are not the test bank's answer explanations and do not cover every question type.

faq_items.question: Does a better practice score mean my IQ increased?
faq_items.answer: Not by itself. Familiarity with items and methods can affect retest performance. Record what changed in your approach and conditions, and use new material to check a strategy; a score increase alone does not establish a change in general intelligence.
